sections.en: 2 παραγίνεται ('is present') M. 3 is it not τῆς παρὰ γυναικῶν διαγωγῆς ('of the conduct concerning women')? namely, not prone to venereal desires. 5 he decrees marriages of unworthy women, Firmicus, in whom also all the rest are found. 8 perhaps σεσινωμέναις ('damaged'), προσώποις ('faces'). 9 πανοτεκνία ἢ κραδυτεκνία ('all-childbearing or slow-childbearing') M. 10 truly ψυκτικὰ ('cooling') or ψυχρὰ ('cold') (they will always be cold to Venus, Firmicus). 11 εὐεπίβολος ('successful') Valens. 13 τινὸς χρόνου ('of some time') Valens wrote, if he wrote it: ἐπί τινας χρόνους ('for some times') Marc. 314 has. 15-19 almost the same in Firmicus. 19 περίεργοι ('curious')] their nature ... will be imbued with the studies of many disciplines, Firmicus. 22 do not [read] δωροληψίας ('of taking bribes') cf. 178, 14. 25 sq. καὶ αὐτὴ ('and she herself') is suspected. 30 wickedness is prohibited, Firmicus. 35-164, 16 very similar in Firmicus. 67v b.

summary.headline: Saturn with Venus, Mercury, and Moon
summary.text: Astrological delineations of Saturn joined with Venus, Mercury, and the Moon, covering marriage, childlessness, deceit, disease, maternal life, possessions, and the differing effects of nocturnal and diurnal sect. Valens is cited for parallel interpretations, and the passage begins Saturn trine Jupiter as a configuration for wealth.
